ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, there is a circle with K as the center, and M, L, N, and J are all on the circle. The blue straight line L-P-K-J passes through the center K, so it is the line on which the diameter lies; this line intersects chord MN at P, and there is a right-angle mark in the figure, indicating that it is perpendicular to chord MN. L is located on the shorter arc MN, and J is located on the longer arc MN. Given m arc MN = 98. A diameter passing through the center and perpendicular to a chord bisects the two arcs cut off by that chord. Therefore J is the midpoint of the major arc MN. The measure of the major arc MN is 360 - 98 = 262. Thus m arc NJ = 262 ÷ 2 = 131. Rounded to the nearest hundredth, it is still 131.

raw_record.question_text: $\ln \odot K$, $MN=16$ and $m\widehat{MN}=98$. Find the measure of $m\widehat{NJ}$. Round to the nearest hundredth.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: points M, L, N, J lie on circle K, and the blue line through L, P, K, J passes through the center K. It meets chord MN at P with a right-angle mark, so this line is a diameter/radius line perpendicular to chord MN. From the text, use m arc MN = 98 and the target is m arc NJ. Since a diameter perpendicular to a chord bisects both arcs cut off by the chord, J is the midpoint of the major arc MN, while L is on the minor arc. The major arc MN has measure 360 - 98 = 262, so arc NJ is half of that: 262/2 = 131.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a central-angle configuration: K is the center, MN is a chord, and the line KJ is on the perpendicular bisector of chord MN because it passes through K and is perpendicular to MN at P. From the text, the minor arc MN is 98 degrees, so the minor central angle between KM and KN is 98 degrees. The reflex central angle from KM around the major arc to KN is 360 - 98 = 262 degrees. Because KJ lies on the perpendicular bisector/symmetry axis of chord MN, ray KJ bisects this reflex central angle. Therefore angle NKJ is 262/2 = 131 degrees, and the measure of arc NJ equals its central angle, 131 degrees.
